answer: Scarce Mirror Seats.** Each identity must be anchored to a distinct verified action channel, and every channel broadcasts a signed mirror of its recent coordination graph. Identities whose graphs overlap above a fixed threshold share one seat, priced by a pigment marker in the registry that records reuse. An attacker paying for N identities pays for N disjoint channels plus separation costs to keep their mirrors distinct; once flagged, all linked identities collapse into a single seat and forfeit their remaining channel rents.
